name: Sebastian Selman
tagline: I work on the gap between what technology can do and what organisations manage to do with it.
intro: That gap is mostly not technical. It shows up as a data platform nobody trusts, a governance model written for a world that no longer exists, or an AI pilot that works beautifully and changes nothing. I spend my time on the organisational side of that problem — currently in enterprise data engineering and data governance, previously across Microsoft's Azure data and AI portfolio, and before that as a design-thinking consultant working with banks and healthcare on how they actually make decisions.

I teach some of this: four years lecturing on digital corporate culture at BVS St. Gallen, and a run of workshops and sessions with universities and fellowship programmes. I co-host a podcast about what happens when enterprises put AI into production, and I write — sometimes about Azure and data architecture, sometimes about borders, personas and why IKEA sells hot dogs.
I grew up in Baden-Baden, was born in Toronto, and started my working life as assistant to a violin maker in Tübingen. Some of that turns out to be more relevant than it sounds.
publishing_note: Earlier essays and articles appear under my former publishing name, Sebastian Rappen.
